clue.text: First two things haplessly tried — I'm disregarding poor start, having courage!

definitions.text: First two things haplessly tried — I'm disregarding poor start, having courage!

parts.note: the first two letters of the word things

indicators.note: a hapless attempt goes awry, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: to disregard something is to leave it out, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: someone with courage is plucky

indicators.note: the start of the word poor is its first letter alone

parts.note: its first letter is the one dropped

explanation.surface: After two failed attempts, the speaker scorns a bad beginning and summons the nerve to try once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the saying: two tries have failed, so the next is expected to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that after two failures a third attempt will succeed, which is exactly the situation the clue describes.

clue.text: Maestro account among three in circulation

indicators.note: the account abbreviation sits among the other letters
letters going round in circulation are stirred into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A conductor's account is passed around among three people.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, often a distinguished music teacher, so the words are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: One runs attached to bloke for three-legged race

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
something attached is on, as a lid is on a jar
British slang for a man

explanation.surface: A runner is tied to a man for a three-legged race at a school sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-legged race here is not the sack-and-string sports day event but a triathlon, whose three legs are swimming, cycling and running.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironman is a long-distance triathlon, a race with three stages or legs.

clue.text: Cleaned kettle spattered with bits of tea and prevented from boiling over

indicators.note: spattered drops scatter everywhere, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: removing limescale from a kettle is descaling it
the letters of the word tea, scattered among the others

explanation.surface: A freshly descaled kettle gets splashed with tea, and stops it bubbling over.
explanation.walkthrough: Boiling over is figurative: a dispute kept from escalating has been de-escalated.
explanation.definitionFit: To de-escalate a conflict is to calm it down before it erupts, figuratively stopping it boiling over.

clue.text: If Jack takes 3rd place, guaranteed to get hurt

indicators.note: Jack takes over the third letter's position, replacing what was there

parts.note: something insured is covered or guaranteed against loss

explanation.surface: If a jockey called Jack finishes third, he is sure to be hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been hurt is injured; the two past participles are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Requires guts to oust royal

indicators.note: ousting someone throws them out, so that letter goes

parts.note: entrails are the guts or intestines

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a monarch takes nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: If one thing entails another, it necessarily involves or needs it.

clue.text: See 1
See 11 Across
Foamy head on coffee/tea, without a burn

parts.note: crema is the golden foam on top of an espresso

indicators.note: tea without the letter a, which is left out

parts.note: taken as written
the letter A, taken as written

explanation.surface: A frothy coffee or a tea, minus a scald.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate a body is to burn it to ashes, so the verb is a specific kind of burning.

clue.text: 'Ramsey' misspelling garners a thousand whinges

indicators.note: to garner is to gather in, so the thousand is taken inside
a misspelt name has its letters in the wrong order

parts.note: the setter's own name, misspelt in the surface
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: The setter Ramsay grumbles that a thousand people misspell the name as Ramsey.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to complain loudly and at length, much as a moaner whinges.

clue.text: Swapped walls of daub in mudbrick house

indicators.note: the two letters trade places within the word
the outer letters of daub, D and B, are the pair that change places

parts.note: adobe is sun-dried mud brick

explanation.surface: Mud plaster daubed on the walls of a mudbrick house.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a home or dwelling, a formal word for where one lives.

clue.text: Current mishap of setter in spot of bother

indicators.note: the jumbled setter goes in the spot of bother

parts.note: being in a jam is being in trouble

indicators.note: a mishap knocks these letters out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The crossword setter's latest accident leaves him in some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Current is a noun here: a flow of air, not something up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet stream is a fast, narrow current of air high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Metal wreckage after helicopter tragedy

indicators.note: the shuffled metal comes after the helicopter letter

parts.note: H marks a helicopter landing pad

indicators.note: wrecked metal is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Twisted metal after a helicopter crash marks a real tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tragedy is not the crash but a play: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Danish prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is one of Shakespeare's most famous tragedies, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Something guaranteed, that is incorporating fact I managed to get qualification

parts.note: a cert is a racing term for a sure thing

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is takes the shuffled letters into its body
managed letters have been handled and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sure thing: the speaker managed a fact and earned a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate is the document awarded for passing a course, so it stands for a qualification.

clue.text: Ever supreme, furiously led with ambition

indicators.note: furious action churns these letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone always on top, driven furiously by ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone indomitable can never be beaten or subdued, so remains forever unconquered.

clue.text: Rolling first joint, dopehead rubbed the wrong way!

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Rolling

parts.note: its initial letter is taken
the ankle is the joint between leg and foot
the head of the word dope is its first letter

explanation.surface: A stoner rolling up the first joint of the day irritates someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint points to cannabis in the surface but here it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles annoys or irritates persistently, the same as rubbing someone the wrong way.

clue.text: Blues and dancing featured in clip of session

indicators.note: the jumbled word appears inside the shortened word
clipping session cuts off its ending

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blues band and dancers appear in a short video of a jam session.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the blues means feeling low, so sadness is the state of melancholy the plural noun names.

clue.text: Reads aloud and translates for the audience?

indicators.note: what an audience hears is the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: to translate is also to move from one place to another, that is to resite

explanation.surface: A performer reads out a text and interprets it for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Translate has an old sense of relocate, used of bishops moved to a new see or relics shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to speak a passage out loud, typically from memory or a page.

clue.text: Communist party admitted newspaper revolved around spies

indicators.note: the communists let the reversed paper in among them

parts.note: reds are communists as a group

indicators.note: the paper is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A communist faction let a newspaper in, then turned against agents snooping on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at or observe, so it shares the verb sense of spies, meaning catches sight of.

clue.text: Blimey, pinching bottom is less civilised

indicators.note: pinching grips something, so one part holds the other

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
arse is British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Exclaiming and pinching someone's behind is boorish behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarser means cruder or more vulgar, the comparative of a word for unrefined manners.

clue.text: Sucking up / swallowing six

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the numeral goes in

parts.note: the forward stroke character is called a slash
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Choosing between grovelling and gulping down six things.
explanation.walkthrough: The stroke is not punctuation dividing two options but a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish behaviour is servile and fawning, like a person sucking up to a superior.

clue.text: Discovered Cuban music and heavy metal, as forgotten

indicators.note: read as the plural of the letter A, both of which are forgotten: one A drops from each word

parts.note: rumba is a Cuban dance rhythm
lead is a notably heavy metal

explanation.surface: Someone discovered both Cuban music and heavy metal, both now forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: As here means two letter A's, one from each word; heavy metal is not the music genre.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rumbled is British slang for being found out or seen through.

clue.text: Emerging from green terrace, go back in

indicators.note: the answer emerges from within the letters of these words

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the two words

explanation.surface: Stepping out from a green terrace, then going back inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to come back into a place, the same as returning inside.

clue.text: Express anger and cry after a little bit of singing

indicators.note: after means the cry comes later in the answer than the bit of singing

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale, a tiny snatch of song
to shout is to cry out

explanation.surface: Someone vents fury by yelling once a song has started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little bit of singing' looks like a letter pick but is a whole note: la, from do-re-mi. 'after' puts the cry behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to attack suddenly in words or blows, an idiom for venting temper.

clue.text: Without getting emotional, adored every other piece involving French pop

indicators.note: the alternate letters enclose the French pop
every second letter of adored is kept

parts.note: its alternate letters are used
yé-yé is the 1960s French pop style

explanation.surface: An unemotional fan, once devoted to every other French pop song.
explanation.walkthrough: Yé-yé was the bubbly French pop of the 1960s, from the English yeah yeah.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dry-eyed means shedding no tears, staying unmoved where others might cry.

clue.text: Elder fellow carries foreign currency with equal value

indicators.note: the gentleman carries the other pieces inside him

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow
the rand is South Africa's currency
par means level or equal value

explanation.surface: An older man carries foreign cash of matching worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandparent is one of the older generation in a family, an elder relative.

clue.text: Latin continent and Spanish state

parts.note: SA is South America, the Latin American continent
y is Spanish for and

explanation.surface: A Latin American country and a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: State is a verb here, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to declare it, so the verb is a synonym of say.

clue.text: Check temperature after period of chill weather

indicators.note: the temperature letter comes after the rest

parts.note: chilling out is resting, so a rest is time spent relaxing
rain is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: Take the temperature after a spell of cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is a check or curb on action, as when holding something back.

clue.text: Butter or jam

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to cram or force something in

explanation.walkthrough: Butter is read as one that butts, not the dairy spread, so the breakfast table is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is a male sheep known for butting, and to ram something in is to jam it hard.

clue.text: Shocking cry from bird

parts.note: boo is the cry that startles someone
by can mean from, as in a letter by someone

explanation.surface: An alarming squawk coming from a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The booby is a tropical seabird related to the gannet.

clue.text: Go away from pack, pursuing south

indicators.note: the cram piece follows the compass letter, as a pursuer comes behind

parts.note: to cram is to pack tightly

explanation.surface: Leaving a group of animals, chasing southward.
explanation.walkthrough: Pack is a verb here, not a group of wolves.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command telling someone to leave at once.

clue.text: Brought in the crops but, tragically, he starved

indicators.note: a tragic turn throws these letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The farmer got the harvest in, yet sadly still went hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvested means gathered in when ripe, exactly what is done with crops at harvest time.
